Thanks for sharing these options! My price range is a bit limited—I’m hoping to stay between $15 and $30. Based on that, "Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver" seems like it might fit. 

Could you tell me more about "Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver"? I’m curious about what makes it an interesting read.
dialogue.agent:
"Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver" ($19.95) is a thoroughly researched biography of James B. Weaver, a significant but often overlooked 19th-century American politician. Weaver ran for president twice, led progressive movements like the Greenback-Labor and Populist parties, and advocated for ideas such as government control of railroads, income tax reform, and direct senatorial elections. The book provides a panoramic look at major historical events—from the Gold Rush and Civil War to the rise of William Jennings Bryan—and highlights how Weaver bridged the Victorian and Gilded Ages into the 20th century.

Winner of the 2009 Benjamin F. Shambaugh Award, the book is praised for bringing to life both the political intrigue of the era and Weaver’s personal journey. One reviewer notes that the author’s vivid research makes the complexities of the time engaging, and that Weaver’s influence on third-party politics and social progress is important for anyone interested in political history. Would you like to know more or see other options?

result.title: Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver
result.features: Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver tells the story of a 19th-century politician whose two campaigns for the White House helped change the course of American politics. Weaver served three terms in Congress and ran twice for president, once as the nominee of the Greenback-Labor Party in 1880 and again as the Populist nominee in 1892, when he carried four states. He supported government ownership of the railroads, changes in monetary policy, a graduated income tax, and the direct election of senators. Deeply held religious principles guided Weaver s approach to politics, which he saw as a means of putting the principles of the Galilean in motion among men. This book, the first full-length biography of Weaver in almost 90 years, offers the reader a panoramic view of some of the great events of the 19th century the California Gold Rush, the Civil War, and presidential politics from the election of Abraham Lincoln in 1860 to the rise of William Jennings Bryan in 1896. Skirmisher also sheds new light on the role of religion in American politics and the influence of third parties in presidential elections. Winner of the 2009 Benjamin F. Shambaugh Award from the State Historical Society of Iowa. This annual award recognizes the book judged as the most significant book on Iowa history for the year.

top_reviews.title: Political Outsider
top_reviews.text:
The political times of the Victorian and Gilded Ages in our country are somewhat forgotten and obscure. But that does not make them uninteresting. Politically, they were surprisingly fast moving. And eventful. There were two Presidential assassinations. There were near wars, invasions, a mini depression.

And while, historically, the political landscape between Ullyses Grant and Theodore Roosevelt seems bland and colorless. In retrospect, there were some colorful ideas.

James Weaver was a little giant of his times. Being a leader of political ideology, a political force, and a tireless campaigner, he bridged the aforementioned Victorian and Gilded age into the modern 20th century. His run as both Populist and Greenback candidates gave voice to a third party, and brought about the gravitas for both Eugene Debs and William Jennings Bryan candidacies.

A strong but flawed character, he also was one of the first candidates to to have a strong woman presence at the front of his campaign.

The author, Robert Mitchell, brings the times to life in his vivid research and writing of the life and times of James Weaver. Significant from the Civil War, where he rose to the rank of colonel, spanning to 1912, where he threw his support behind, and influenced Woodrow Wilson, Weaver is a historical figure most have have never heard of.

For the those with interest in the politics of these times, this is an important read.

I know it’s listed for $12.99, which is a little below my ideal minimum, but I want to see how it compares in terms of story and appeal, since I do enjoy mysteries.
dialogue.agent:
"Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)" ($12.99) is a highly-rated mystery featuring Amanda Warren, who’s on a getaway in North Carolina when she’s called back to New Jersey—her daughter is being questioned in a murder case involving a famous TV finance guru. The suspense builds as Amanda, with her partner Jace and his former NYPD partner, tries to clear her daughter’s name while uncovering ties to a dangerous international drug cartel.

A reviewer praises Amanda as a relatable and vulnerable protagonist, navigating personal struggles while solving mysteries. The review highlights engaging twists, fun, and a touch of romance as Amanda uncovers clues in the Jersey Shore setting.

Would you like help choosing between "Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)" and "Skirmisher: The Life, Times, and Political Career of James B. Weaver," or is there something else you’d like to know?

result.title: Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)
result.features: Amanda Warren's Next Murder...Amanda and Jace are spending a blissful week in North Carolina when her daughter Katie calls-- she's being held for questioning in the murder of popular TV finance guru Kevin Patterson. They rush back to New Jersey, where Amanda meets Jace's beautiful ex-NYPD partner, Lori Malone, the detective who's holding Katie for questioning. This case is out of Jace's jurisdiction but he and Amanda must find the killer to clear Katie's name. The stakes rise quickly as they unearth Patterson's connection to a powerful international drug cartel. Can Amanda and Jace find the killer-- and clear Katie's name-- before someone kills them first?

top_reviews.title: What could be worse than having your own daughter held under suspicion of ...
top_reviews.text:
What could be worse than having your own daughter held under suspicion of murder? Not trusting the cop you love to keep an objective viewpoint when an old flame turns up, that's what!

Amanda Warren grows on you. She's very human, and somehow vulnerable as she forges a new life for herself after a bitter divorce. Everything would be great, in fact, except for the unsolved murders that keep cropping up around her. Grab yourself a Blood Orange dessert, and get in on the fun and romance as Amanda works her magic on another Jersey Shore mystery. You'll love it!
